extra.message: Code Injection via eval() in patient_formula_cast_256 — Arbitrary Python code execution, full server compromise. [verified: Same as findings 2/15: user-controlled `expr` passed to `eval()` with bypassable sandbox; introspection chains enable arbitrary code execution.]

Code Injection via eval() with bypassable sandbox — Remote code execution on the server [verified: User-controlled `expr` is passed to `eval()` with empty `__builtins__`; the sandbox is trivially bypassable via Python introspection chains (e.g., `().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()`), enabling arbitrary code execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 in patient_jinja_cast_490 — Remote code execution, arbitrary file read, and full access to Django settings including SECRET_KEY and database credentials. [verified: Same as findings 0/14: user-controlled `fragment` concatenated into Jinja2 `Template().render()` with no sanitization; SSTI enables arbitrary code execution.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in patient_dock_shelf_496 — Arbitrary file write anywhere on the filesystem, enabling code execution via overwriting Python files, cron jobs, or SSH authorized_keys. [verified: Same as finding 4: user-controlled `name` joined to `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` via `/` with no path sanitization; `target.parent.mkdir(parents=True)` creates directories, enabling arbitrary file write.]

OS Command Injection via ping in patient_shell_probe_508 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process, enabling data theft, lateral movement, or system compromise. [verified: Same as findings 1/13: user-controlled `host` concatenated into `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` with no sanitization; shell metacharacters enable arbitrary command execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — Remote code execution on the server; full system compromise [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `fragment` is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string via `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` with no sanitization; _wrk_gate is authentication, not a control that neutralizes SSTI.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 in patient_jinja_cast_490 — Arbitrary code execution, reading of server-side secrets and configuration, full server compromise. [verified: Same as finding 0: user-controlled `fragment` concatenated into `Template("Result: " + fragment).render()` with no sanitization; Jinja2 SSTI enables arbitrary code execution.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write — Arbitrary file write leading to code execution or system compromise [verified: User-controlled `name` is joined to `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` via `/` operator with no path sanitization; `name=../../etc/cron.d/evil` escapes the directory and `target.parent.mkdir(parents=True)` creates intermediate directories, enabling arbitrary file write.]

Command Injection via os.system in patient_shell_probe_508 — Remote code execution on the server, full system compromise. [verified: Same as finding 1: user-controlled `host` concatenated into `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` with no sanitization; shell metacharacters enable arbitrary command execution.]

OS Command Injection via os.system — Remote code execution on the server [verified: User-controlled GET parameter `host` is concatenated directly into `os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)` with no escaping, validation, or sanitization; shell metacharacters allow arbitrary command execution.]

Hardcoded Default Django SECRET_KEY Enables Session Forgery and Account Takeover — Session forgery, CSRF bypass, password reset token forgery, full account takeover for any user. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY default on settings.py line 8 as finding 0; 'dev-only-change-me' is used when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset with zero compensating controls anywhere in the codebase, enabling session forgery and account takeover.]

Hardcoded Fallback Django SECRET_KEY — Session forgery, CSRF bypass, password reset token forgery [verified: settings.py line 8 hardcodes a well-known default SECRET_KEY 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var is absent; no runtime check, separate production config, or deployment override exists anywhere in the repository to prevent this default from being used in production, enabling session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery.]

Hardcoded Database Credentials Fallback — Unauthorized database access with default credentials [verified: settings.py lines 48-50 hardcode default database credentials 'clinic_portal' for NAME, USER, and PASSWORD when the corresponding POSTGRES_* env vars are absent; no separate production config or runtime validation exists, granting full database access with well-known defaults if deployed without environment configuration.]

Hardcoded Default Database Credentials — Full unauthorized access to the PostgreSQL database containing all patient PII, clinical data, prescriptions, audit logs, and user credentials if the service is network-accessible. [verified: Same hardcoded database password 'clinic_portal' on settings.py line 49 as findings 3 and 6; combined with default username and DB name, full database access is possible with well-known credentials if POSTGRES_PASSWORD is not explicitly set in the environment.]

IDOR: Clinician can self-book appointments for any patient to gain unauthorized access to their full medical records — A clinician can escalate privileges by creating an appointment with any patient as themselves the provider, which bypasses the patient-scoping in _visible_patients and makes can_view_patient return True, granting full access to PII, clinical data, prescriptions, documents, and messages for any patient in the system. [verified: appointment_create line 222 only checks patient==appt.patient for PATIENT role; clinicians bypass this entirely. AppointmentForm.__init__ leaves patient queryset unrestricted for clinicians, and can_view_patient returns True for clinicians with any appointment — a self-booked appointment grants full chart access to any patient.]

Authorization bypass — prescription persisted before access control check — A clinician can create unauthorized prescriptions for patients they have no clinical relationship with (different provider assignment, no shared appointments). The prescription record is permanently written to the database with attacker-controlled medication_name, dosage, instructions, and status, polluting patient clinical records and potentially enabling downstream clinical workflow abuse. [verified: prescription_create line 337 calls form.save() before the can_edit_clinical check at line 338; Django's default autocommit commits the INSERT, and raising PermissionDenied does not roll back. No ATOMIC_REQUESTS or transaction.atomic wrapper exists.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in patient_xml_fold_520 — Arbitrary local file disclosure (e.g., /etc/passwd, environment files, source code), server-side request forgery to internal services, and potential denial of service via billion laughs attack. [verified: Same as findings 3/16: lxml parser with `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False` parses raw request body; XXE enables file read and SSRF.]

NoSQL Injection via pymongo in patient_mongo_lane_539 — Unauthorized data access from MongoDB, denial of service via resource-intensive queries, and potential JavaScript code execution on the database server. [verified: Same as findings 5/17: user-controlled JSON body passed as MongoDB query to `find_one()`; NoSQL operators enable query bypass with no validation.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection — Arbitrary file read, server-side request forgery, potential denial of service [verified: lxml XMLParser is initialized with `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False` and parses raw `request.body`; external entity declarations can read local files or perform SSRF with no validation.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via unsafe lxml parser in patient_xml_fold_520 — Arbitrary file read of server files including secrets, SSRF to internal services, denial of service. [verified: Same as finding 3: lxml parser configured with `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False` parses raw request body; external entities enable file read and SSRF.]

NoSQL Injection via pymongo — Unauthorized data access, data exfiltration, denial of service [verified: User-controlled JSON body is used as the MongoDB query filter via `query = payload.get("filter", payload)` then `find_one(query)`; NoSQL operators like `{"$gt": ""}` or `{"$where": "..."}` bypass record filtering with no input validation.]

DEBUG=True by Default Exposes Sensitive Configuration and Patient Data — Exposure of SECRET_KEY, database credentials, INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN, stack traces, and unauthenticated access to uploaded patient documents via media URL. [verified: Same DEBUG=True default on settings.py line 9 as finding 1; no production override exists and urls.py conditionally serves media files exposing patient documents and error pages with stack traces and configuration secrets to any visitor.]

DEBUG=True by Default Exposes Sensitive Information and Media Files — Public exposure of Django SECRET_KEY (enabling session forgery), database credentials, full stack traces, all uploaded patient documents (medical records, insurance cards, lab reports), and internal application state. [verified: Same DEBUG=True default on settings.py line 9 as findings 1 and 5; no production override, and the urls.py DEBUG gate on line 18 exposes all uploaded media (medical documents, insurance cards) and detailed Django error pages with SECRET_KEY and credentials to unauthenticated visitors.]

DEBUG=True by Default with Media Exposure — Public access to uploaded medical documents, stack traces exposing sensitive configuration and code paths [verified: settings.py line 9 defaults DEBUG=True via `os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG','1')=='1'`; no production guard or conditional override exists, and urls.py line 18 serves MEDIA files publicly when DEBUG is True, exposing uploaded patient documents and detailed error stack traces with secrets to any visitor.]

Mass Assignment of Security-Sensitive Fields in PatientDemographicsForm — A patient can change their assigned primary clinician (potentially to a complicit provider), or toggle their own active status, bypassing administrative controls over patient-provider assignments. [verified: Same root cause as Findings 0 and 2: PatientDemographicsForm unconditionally includes is_active and primary_clinician; patient_edit permits self-edit, so a patient can POST arbitrary values for both privileged fields.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Attackers can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing against user accounts, unlimited username enumeration via registration timing, and abuse the password reset flow to spam users with reset emails. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware (django-axes, django-ratelimit, django-defender) is installed; register (line 85), login (LoginView), and password_reset endpoints are all reachable with unlimited attempts, enabling brute-force and enumeration.]

CSV Formula Injection in Appointment Export — Arbitrary command execution when exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet software [verified: export_appointments (line 504) writes appt.reason directly via csv.writer with no formula-trigger prefix stripping or cell escaping; AppointmentForm has no clean_reason validator. Attacker-controlled reason reaches CSV sink unsanitized.]

CSV Formula Injection in appointment export — Remote code execution on the machine of any staff member who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application. An attacker can craft a malicious appointment reason that executes OS commands when the CSV is opened. [verified: Same as finding 1: export_appointments writes user-controlled appt.reason to CSV via csv.writer with no formula-character sanitization; no clean_reason validator on AppointmentForm.]

must_change_password Flag Not Enforced — Imported users retain weak/guessable passwords indefinitely [verified: UserProfile.must_change_password is set to True at line 603 in import_patients but is never checked by any middleware, view decorator, login signal, or template — the field exists with zero enforcement paths.]

must_change_password Flag Set But Never Enforced — Imported patients with unusable passwords cannot log in and are never prompted to set a password, breaking the account provisioning workflow. If passwords were set, the security requirement of forced password change is silently ignored. [verified: Duplicate of finding 2: must_change_password=True is set at line 603 with no enforcement (no middleware, decorator, signal, or template check). Additionally, set_unusable_password() at line 601 creates users who cannot authenticate at all, with no recovery flow.]

API Key Exposed via GET Query Parameter — API key leakage through logs, browser history, and Referer headers [verified: line 644 accepts API key via request.GET.get('api_key') as fallback to X-API-Key header; no control prevents GET-param acceptance. Keys in URL query strings leak via server access logs, browser history, proxy logs, and Referer headers.]

API Key Accepted via GET Query Parameter Leading to Credential Leakage — API key exposure through server logs, browser history, and Referer headers, enabling unauthorized access to the availability API. [verified: Same as finding 0: line 644 accepts API key via request.GET.get('api_key') with no header-only enforcement, exposing keys through logs, history, and Referer headers.]

No Rate Limiting on Internal Ops Token Enabling Brute-Force — An attacker can perform unlimited brute-force attempts against the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN, and upon success gains access to 18 ops endpoints containing command injection, SSTI, XXE, NoSQL injection, path traversal, and code execution sinks—leading to full server compromise. [verified: No rate limiting, lockout, backoff, or audit logging exists on _wrk_gate (lines 19-22) or anywhere in the Django middleware stack; all 19 /ops/* endpoints are reachable and gated solely by this unprotected token comparison, enabling unlimited brute-force attempts without detection.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) — Session hijacking, credential theft, page defacement [verified: User-controlled `copyline` from GET is concatenated directly into an HTML string `

" + copyline + "

...` returned with `content_type="text/html"`; no HTML escaping, enabling reflected XSS behind the ops token gate.]

Open Redirect — Phishing, credential theft, session token leakage via Referer header [verified: User-controlled `lane` from GET/POST is passed directly to Django's `redirect(lane)` with no URL validation; `redirect()` follows any URL including external domains, enabling open redirect for token holders.]

Log Injection and Sensitive Auth Token Logging — Log forgery, authentication token leakage through application logs [verified: `logger.warning("ops tally body=%s bearer=%s", body, request.headers.get("authorization"))` writes the Authorization header to application logs at WARNING level; sensitive tokens are exposed in logs accessible to operators and log aggregation systems.]

Sensitive Data (Bearer Tokens) Written to Logs in patient_wire_tally_216 — Exposure of authentication tokens, session identifiers, and potentially patient PII in application logs, compromising confidentiality and enabling account takeover. [verified: Same as findings 11/20: Authorization header logged at WARNING level; sensitive tokens exposed in application logs.]

SSL/TLS Certificate Verification Disabled — Man-in-the-middle attacks, data interception, injection of malicious responses [verified: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` disables TLS certificate verification on outbound HTTPS; though the hardcoded target `partner.invalid` is non-resolvable, SSL verification is genuinely disabled on a reachable code path, enabling MITM if the endpoint were pointed at a real host.]

SSL Certificate Verification Disabled in Outbound HTTPS Request — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections, enabling interception of sensitive data sent to external partners. [verified: Same as finding 10: `ssl._create_unverified_context()` disables TLS verification; reachable code path with disabled certificate validation, though target is non-resolvable `.invalid` domain.]

Missing Secure Flag on Session and CSRF Cookies — Session hijacking via network sniffing on insecure networks, enabling complete account takeover of any authenticated user whose cookies are intercepted. [verified: Both SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are absent from settings.py (confirmed zero matches in entire codebase); cookies lack the Secure flag and can be intercepted over unencrypted HTTP despite the configured SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER, enabling session hijacking via MITM.]

Missing SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE Flag Allows Session Cookie Transmission Over HTTP — Session cookies can be intercepted over unencrypted HTTP connections, enabling session hijacking and account takeover via network-level attacks. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is never set to True in the entire codebase (confirmed by exhaustive search); without this flag, session cookies transmit over plain HTTP enabling network-level session hijacking even though SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is configured.]

Missing Secure Cookie Flags — Session and CSRF token theft over unencrypted connections [verified: Neither SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE nor CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE is set to True anywhere in settings.py or the entire codebase (confirmed by zero grep matches); SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER alone does not set the Secure flag, so cookies will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, vulnerable to network sniffing.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Brute-force password attacks, credential stuffing, account enumeration [verified: No rate-limiting library installed (requirements.txt), no throttling middleware (settings.py), and vanilla LoginView/PasswordResetView (urls.py line 8) lack any decorator or attempt-tracking — brute-force is unconstrained on a reachable unauthenticated endpoint.]

User Enumeration via Distinct Username Availability Error in Registration — An attacker can compile a list of valid usernames for targeted brute-force attacks, credential stuffing, or social engineering. [verified: Same clean_username distinct-error pattern as Finding 1; no rate-limiting on the registration endpoint, so an attacker can iterate usernames and receive deterministic availability signals.]

Account enumeration via registration username check — An unauthenticated attacker can enumerate valid usernames in the healthcare portal, enabling targeted password guessing, credential stuffing, or social-engineering attacks against identified patients and clinicians. [verified: clean_username in PatientRegistrationForm returns a distinct 'That username is already registered.' error when the username exists; no rate-limiting middleware or view-level throttling is configured on /register/, enabling unauthenticated enumeration.]

Mass Assignment: VisitSummary status Field Bypasses Release Workflow — Visit summaries can be marked as released without audit trail or proper patient notification, potentially exposing draft clinical information to patients prematurely. [verified: VisitSummaryForm.Meta.fields includes status with no __init__ override to exclude it; a clinician posting to visit_summary_edit can set status=RELEASED directly, skipping VisitSummary.release() which would set released_at, notify the patient, and log a release audit entry—though clinicians are already authorized to release summaries.]

Hardcoded Demo Password in Seed Command — An attacker who obtains the source code or triggers the seed command can authenticate as any demo user (including admin) using the known password DemoPass123!, leading to full patient data compromise and account takeover. [verified: The password 'DemoPass123!' is genuinely hardcoded at line 33 of seed_clinic.py with no production guard (no DEBUG check, no confirmation prompt) and the CLI entry point is reachable per the threat model. However, exploitation requires either shell access to run the management command (which implies deeper compromise) or accidental execution in a non-demo environment combined with source-code leak]

Missing Authentication on Ops Endpoint patient_identity_ping_339 — Unauthenticated access to an operations endpoint that processes and reflects user input, enabling information gathering and potential abuse as an open relay. [verified: Same as finding 12: `patient_identity_ping_339` lacks `_wrk_gate` check present on all other ops endpoints; gate genuinely absent, though impact limited to echoing non-sensitive parameters.]

CORS Misconfiguration with Credentials in patient_origin_mirror_469 — Cross-origin data theft — any website can make credentialed requests to this endpoint and read responses, enabling CSRF-style attacks that exfiltrate sensitive JSON responses. [verified: Same as findings 8/19: CORS mirrors Origin with credentials=true; genuine misconfiguration on endpoint returning only non-sensitive origin data.]

Missing Authentication Gate on Ops Endpoint — Unauthenticated access to internal operations endpoint [verified: `patient_identity_ping_339` has no `_wrk_gate(request)` check, unlike all other 18 ops endpoints; the gate is genuinely absent, though current impact is limited to echoing non-sensitive `handle` and `channel` parameters.]

Permissive CORS with Credentials — Cross-origin data theft, session hijacking via malicious websites [verified: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reflects the request `Origin` header and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is set; genuine CORS misconfiguration exists, but the endpoint returns only non-sensitive `{"origin": "..."}` with no user data to exfiltrate.]

Permissive CORS Configuration Mirrors Request Origin with Credentials — Cross-origin data theft by malicious websites reading sensitive responses using the victim's authenticated session. [verified: Same as finding 8: CORS reflects Origin with credentials=true; genuine misconfiguration but endpoint exposes only non-sensitive `{"origin":"..."}` data.]
